messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Priyanka Sharma <priyanka.sharma@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Performance SLO checklist & next steps

Hi Alex / Priyanka —

Thanks again for giving us 45 mins today — great conversation and appreciate you walking us through the production traffic profile. Per our demo goals, I captured a short Performance/SLO checklist so we can confirm alignment and identify any technical blockers before we scope Dedicated capacity. I attached the SLO_Checklist.xlsx for easy editing.

Key items for confirmation (quick answers requested):
- Latency targets: 99th percentile end-to-end for single-turn text generation (target?)
- Expected throughput: average QPS and peak QPS (sustained)
- Concurrency: average number of concurrent sessions and burst concurrency
- Streaming: do you require streamed partial tokens for UX (yes/no)? If yes, what is the acceptable first-byte latency?
- Model: which model variant do you plan to use in prod (open model name/version)?
- Security: any specific private deployment / KMS requirements we should account for now?

From our side, follow-ups we’ll do next:
- Rishi: map the requests to our Dedicated sizing and provide estimated cost and slot counts
- Neha: prepare a short quantization/throughput note and run a quick perf check on the model you mentioned
- I’ll create a MAP (mutual action plan) and send a calendar invite for the technical review next week

Please reply with the bullet answers above or edit the attached checklist — don’t worry about exact numbers, ballpark is fine and we’ll tighten during the technical review.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachment: SLO_Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet - perf targets / sample payloads)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLO checklist & next steps

Thanks Marissa — great session. Attaching a short latency export from our staging tests (latency-benchmark.pdf). Answers below (ballpark):
- Latency targets: 99p end-to-end <= 250ms for single-turn generator calls (higher allowed for very long sequences)
- Expected throughput: baseline 150 QPS, peak sustained 300 QPS during batch processing windows
- Concurrency: typically ~20 concurrent live sessions, bursts up to 50 for specific campaign launches
- Streaming: yes — we need streaming for partial outputs for our mobile UX. First-byte target <= 120ms when streaming enabled
- Model: planning to start with gpt-small-1.1 (open variant) and consider 4-bit quantized variant if perf is acceptable
- Security: standard SOC2 + customer-managed KMS for key material; will provide the questionnaire after internal review

Also: we have some sample payloads (average token lengths in the attachment) — hope that helps you size. Let us know if you want a small test harness or synthetic load generator to run against a staging endpoint.

Best,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com

Attachment: latency-benchmark.pdf (PDF - staging latency export)

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLO checklist & next steps

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the details, Alex — that’s helpful. Quick internal notes / proposed approach:
- Latency: 99p <= 250ms is achievable for short to medium sequences on Dedicated with correct batching and caching. We'll need to validate with the exact payloads and model variant.
- Throughput / Concurrency: baseline 150 QPS (peak 300 QPS) and bursts to 50 concurrent sessions point toward a Dedicated pool of ~6-8 x A100-equivalent slots (estimate). I’ll produce a sizing note with expected per-token cost.
- Streaming: streaming first-byte <= 120ms adds constraints; we’ll want to test end-to-end (runtime + network). Our runtime supports streaming but we should validate the model’s autoregressive token timings for your chosen variant.
- Quantization: Neha — can you run a quick 4-bit perf run for gpt-small-1.1 and report token/s and 95/99p latency numbers? If the loss in quality is small, quantization can reduce slot count.
- Security/KMS: procurement note — if they require customer-managed KMS we’ll route Private onboarding / contract addendum. 

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Rishi: Detailed Dedicated sizing + cost estimate (ETA Mon 03/27)
- Neha: Perf run on gpt-small-1.1 4-bit vs FP16 (ETA Fri 03/24 COB) — will post results to the MAP doc
- Marissa: Prepare MAP + send technical review calendar invite (ETA Fri 03/24)

I’ll draft the sizing doc and share with you both. If we need infra involvement for a staged endpoint, I’ll coordinate.

-Rishi
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
